title: The best soloists in his band: Amos Woodruff, Booker Ervin and Luther West
summary: Melvin Moore was the top singer; for solos he names Amos Woodruff, then Booker Ervin and Luther West.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: I hate to put you on the spot, Ernie, but if you could name the most outstanding instrumentalist--and this will take some time, think about it--that you ever had in your band. Of course I know Melvin Moore would be a hundred percent, hands down, your vote for the greatest singer in the band, and maybe one of the greatest singers anyone ever had. Melvin Moore was one of the greats of history, it's too bad he didn't get the recognition that was due him.
Who would say--if you want to name several, okay, but who stands out as the greatest instrumentalists of your band's career?
Let me pause just a moment.
Well you really hit it right as far as Melvin, as far as vocalists Melvin, but as far as solos, I would say Amos Woodruff.
Then the next two--you said I could name more than one---I would say Booker Irving and Luther West.
They fitted your band, their style?
